verdict_reason: Score above threshold and no blocking issues.

issues.title: zle reset-prompt inside line-pre-redraw hook carries recursion risk not acknowledged
issues.description: The spec specifies that _zah_redraw (a line-pre-redraw hook) calls 'zle reset-prompt' when the hint changes. Calling zle reset-prompt from within a line-pre-redraw hook can trigger a redraw cycle that re-invokes line-pre-redraw hooks in some zsh versions, potentially causing recursion. The spec gates the call behind the _ZAH_LAST_HINT change check (which limits frequency) but does not acknowledge this recursion risk or describe a guard against it (e.g. a reentrancy flag).
issues.suggestion: Add a note under the Service Layer or Edge Cases section acknowledging the zle reset-prompt reentrancy risk and specify the mitigation: either a module-level reentrancy guard (typeset -g _ZAH_IN_RESET=0, checked at entry of _zah_redraw), or explicitly state that the _ZAH_LAST_HINT change gate is sufficient because reset-prompt sets the hint-unchanged path on the recursive invocation.

issues.title: _ZAH_RPROMPT_SAVED capture does not reset between prompts when hint was never activated
issues.description: The spec states _ZAH_RPROMPT_SAVED is captured lazily on first hint activation within _zah_redraw. This is correct across prompts when the hint was activated and then restored (because _ZAH_HINT_ACTIVE is reset to 0 on restore, allowing re-capture on next activation). However the spec does not explicitly describe this re-capture path, which could confuse a developer implementing the lazy-capture logic. The variable description says 'empty until first capture' but does not say 'and re-captured on each new activation after a restore.'
issues.suggestion: In the Data Model Changes section, clarify _ZAH_RPROMPT_SAVED semantics: 'captured lazily at the start of each new hint activation (when _ZAH_HINT_ACTIVE transitions from 0 to 1), allowing it to reflect oh-my-posh's recomputed RPROMPT for each prompt cycle.'

strengths: The kind:defer load-order problem (the prior review's primary blocking issue) is now fully resolved: the spec explains the zsh-defer FIFO queue mechanism, identifies why sourcing at antidote.zsh races against F-Sy-H's deferred load, and commits to a one-shot precmd-guarded registration gating on (( $+functions[_zsh_highlight] )). The approach is architecturally sound and robust against variable deferred-load timing.

The wiring point is corrected to .zshrc after the oh-my-posh block (after line 38), which is the right location: $ZSH_HOME is guaranteed defined, oh-my-posh precmd is installed, and F-Sy-H has not yet loaded (deferring registration to _zah_register is correct).

The zle -N redundancy issue is cleanly resolved: the Registration section explicitly states add-zle-hook-widget takes a plain function name and no zle -N is needed or wanted, with a corrected snippet.
The globalias test gap is resolved: Tier 3 now includes an explicit load-bearing test case asserting hint-gone and no-stale-green after space-triggered globalias expansion.
The $ZSH_HOME availability confirmation is now in the spec (line 102), explicitly referencing .zshrc line 1 and the source point.

F-Sy-H's exclusion of zle-line-pre-redraw from widget wrapping is verified in the actual plugin file (line 242 of fast-syntax-highlighting.plugin.zsh) — this is the crux of why append-after wins, and it is real.
_zsh_highlight is defined at source time (line 66) and resets region_highlight=() at line 74 — both verified, making the _zsh_highlight sentinel and the append-wins theory sound.
No open questions remain — the spec explicitly commits to the precmd-guarded approach as primary and kind:defer local entry as documented fallback.
The contingency plan (chroma/unknown-token override) is correctly positioned as a Tier 2 failure branch, not the primary design.
Performance section correctly identifies zle reset-prompt as the expensive operation and gates it on _ZAH_LAST_HINT change, not per-keystroke.
Catppuccin Mocha color values (#a6e3a1 green, #6c7086 overlay0) verified against oh-my-posh/config.toml [palette].
Scope control is comprehensive: no-gos directly reference CLAUDE.md conventions, out-of-scope list is explicit, rabbit holes pair each with a concrete alternative to avoid.
